title: Numerical bounds at noise x4 require intensity ratios above two in 20 of 126 TESS CPVs under common quadratic limb laws
abstract: Can arbitrary surface spots explain sharp complex periodic variable (CPV) curves with modest intensity differences? We derive bounds for every bounded brightness map on a rigidly rotating sphere. The method permits an unknown flux scale, any surface shape, continuous inclination, and all common monotone physical quadratic limb laws. It uses Fourier error boxes and positive-part support integrals. We apply it to one source-selected TESS sector for each of 126 on-target CPVs. With a fourfold source noise scale and 12 harmonics, the required brightest-to-darkest intensity ratio exceeds two in 20 stars for quadratic laws and 34 for linear laws. The median linear-model lower bound is 1.33. At eightfold noise, 12 stars retain a ratio above two for linear laws; an algebraic quadratic-law relaxation retains three. In 90 stars, the full-curve lower bound exceeds an explicit upper bound for a map of only the broad modulation. A separate dark-map test gives a median required mean flux loss of 4.8%. Exact time integrals, an analytic allowance for continuous inclination, synthetic surface controls, and resolution checks support the calculation. Sphere integration remains numerical. The error model, common limb law, spherical shape, source processing, and selected sectors limit physical inference. These are necessary contrast bounds, not spot temperatures or proof of dust. We provide original code, aggregate evidence, provenance, and scratch-only regeneration.
